title: Test failures on big endian ARMv9 with enable-asm
body:
When building openssl 3.3.3 in a big endian Gentoo VM on an ARMv9 based computer (Radxa Orion O6),
14 tests fail when building with `enable-asm`.  I also get failures in wget (with https) and ssh.  If building with
`no-asm`, then all the problems go away.  So it seems there is some asm code which is not endian clean.

If I build on an ARMv8 machine instead (Nvidia Jetson TX2) then everything works even with `enable-asm`, so presumably it's some asm that is enabled only for newer ARM.

cpu features on Orion O6 (where the tests fail):
```
fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 sve asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb paca pacg dcpodp sve2 sveaes svepmull svebitperm svesha3 svesm4 flagm2 frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh bti ecv afp wfxt
```

cpu features on Jetson TX2 (where the tests succeed):
```
fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 cpuid
```

The tests that fail are the following:

AFALG is not about TCP communication, but AES-CBC encryption done by the kernel.
They use the socket just to pass keys and in/out parameters to the kernel module AFAICT.
It could also be an issue with the kernel headers, or a missing kernel module.
Anyway fortunately completely unrelated to the big-endian assembler issue here.

Ok.  Since the afalg test mentioned aes_cbc, I checked the kernel options for AES.

The kernel for the big endian VM has

```
CONFIG_CRYPTO_AES_ARM64=y
```

but the little endian L0 kernel (which is a vendor kernel) has

```
# CONFIG_CRYPTO_AES_ARM64 is not set
```

so maybe that is the reason for the test fail?
